purpose: A large, categorized corpus of REAL copy mined verbatim from the SFFS website and video pipeline. This is the training corpus the auto-replier and the caption/variant generators learn the brand voice from. Prefer real examples over prose. See brand-voice.md for the distilled principles and hard rules.
audience: K-12 kids and the general short-form 'for you' scroller. Kid-safe: no hard/explicit profanity, though mild slang intensifiers like 'af' are on-brand and allowed.
notes: Everything here is REAL copy pulled from the repos, not invented. ONE exception, recorded on purpose: the 20 `caption` examples had their CLOSING ASK revised on 2026-08-06 when the CTA moved from a comment/follow to the free test. Without it they would have failed the very brand gate they are used to calibrate. Only the ask changed; hooks, rhythm and phrasing are as mined.
The signature device is the binary: praise = Smart Fella, miss = Fart Smella (for now).

LOCKED social rules (see brand-voice.md): concise, funny, Gen Z lowercase-casual, kid-safe (no HARD/explicit profanity, but mild slang intensifiers like 'af' are on-brand and allowed), NO em dashes, at most ONE tasteful emoji, no AI-slop, no over-explaining, always end with a nudge, and make TAKING THE FREE TEST the closing ask (a light comment beat may come before it; do not ask for a follow or subscribe).

Some legacy WEBSITE marketing strings below contain em dashes and en dashes (e.g. a couple of FAQ answers). They are preserved verbatim as mined, but the agent must NOT produce em dashes in generated social copy.
brain+wind emoji glyph is the visual shorthand for SMART/FART and reads as one unit.

explanation-onscreen.description: On-screen answer explanations. Clear, kid-friendly teaching. (This teaching tone is for VIDEO reveals ONLY, never for comment replies.)

examples.text: A robin, sparrow, and eagle are all birds. A salmon is a fish, so it does not belong.
Each number doubles (x2): 3, 6, 12, 24, so the next is 24 x 2 = 48.
The relation is 'get filled in' while the shape stays the same, so the empty square becomes a filled square.
Giant and tiny are opposites, so the opposite of wide is narrow. It's the same relationship, flipped.
An ocean shrinks to a puddle, so a mountain shrinks to a hill. It's the tiny version of the same thing.
The gaps grow +4, +6, +8, +10, so the next gap is +12. That makes 30 + 12 = 42.
Each number is the sum of the two before it: 3 + 5 = 8, so 5 + 8 = 13. It's the Fibonacci pattern.
The sides count up by one: triangle 3, square 4, pentagon 5, so next is the hexagon with 6 sides.
The dot steps clockwise corner to corner: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, then the next corner is bottom-left.
The + secretly means multiply: 4x5=20, 3x6=18, 2x7=14, so 5x4 = 20.

vo-question.description: Question-read narration. Names the category, reads options A-D, calls the timer. Adds spice on hard ones.

examples.text: Question one! Which one does NOT belong? Robin... sparrow... salmon... eagle. Is it A, robin... B, sparrow... C, salmon... or D, eagle? Five seconds, go!
Question two, a number series! Three, six, twelve, twenty-four, and then... what comes next? A, thirty-six... B, forty-eight... C, thirty... or D, forty-two? Five seconds!
Question seven, and this one is tricky! Two, six, twelve, twenty, thirty, and then... what comes next? A, thirty-six... B, forty... C, forty-two... or D, forty-four? Five seconds on the clock!
Question eleven, a shape puzzle! Watch them grow, gaining one side each step: a triangle, then a square, then a pentagon. Which shape comes next?
Last one, question fifteen, a number puzzle, and it's sneaky! If four plus five makes twenty, three plus six makes eighteen, and two plus seven makes fourteen... then five plus four makes... what?

vo-reveal.description: Answer-reveal narration. Warm 'the answer is...' payoff + a one-beat memorable why.

examples.text: The answer is... C, salmon! A robin, a sparrow, and an eagle all soar through the sky as birds. But a salmon? That one swims. It's a fish!
It's... B, forty-eight! Each number simply doubles: three, six, twelve, twenty-four... and twenty-four times two is forty-eight!
The answer is... B, hexagon! Count the sides: triangle three, square four, pentagon five... so next up is the six-sided hexagon!
The answer is... B, thirteen! Add the two numbers before it: five plus eight is thirteen. That's the famous Fibonacci pattern!
The answer is... C, twenty! Here's the trick: that plus sign secretly means multiply. Four times five is twenty, so five times four is twenty too!
It's... B, hill! An ocean shrinks down to a tiny puddle, so a mountain shrinks down to a little hill. Same thing, pocket-sized!
